title: Magnetic Fields due to Electric Current
subject: Physics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Quick Revision

nodes.title: Magnetic Lorentz Force & Cyclotron Motion
points: Lorentz force on a charge q moving with velocity v in electric and magnetic fields: F = q(E + v × B).
Magnetic Lorentz Force: F_m = q(v × B) = qvB sinθ. SI unit of B: Tesla (T = N/(A·m) = Wb/m²). Dimensions: [M¹L⁰T⁻²I⁻¹].
Work done by magnetic force on a charged particle is ALWAYS ZERO (F_m ⊥ v ⟹ dW = F · ds = 0). Hence KE and speed remain CONSTANT.
Circular Trajectory (v ⊥ B, θ = 90°): Magnetic force provides centripetal force: qvB = mv²/r ⟹ Radius r = mv / (qB) = p / (qB) = √(2mE) / (qB).
Time period: T = 2πm / (qB) (independent of speed and radius).
Cyclotron frequency: ν_c = qB / (2πm); Angular cyclotron frequency: ω = qB / m.

nodes.title: Force on Current Conductor & Parallel Wires
points: Force on a straight current-carrying conductor in uniform magnetic field: F = I (L × B) = ILB sinθ.
Direction given by Fleming's Left-Hand Rule or Right-Hand Palm Rule.
Force between two long, straight parallel conductors separated by distance d carrying currents I₁ and I₂: F / L = (μ₀ I₁ I₂) / (2πd).
Attractive vs Repulsive Rule: Parallel currents in the SAME direction ATTRACT each other; currents in OPPOSITE directions REPEL each other.

Standard Definition of Ampere: 1 Ampere is that steady current which, when flowing through two infinitely long straight parallel conductors 1 metre apart in vacuum, produces a force of 2 × 10⁻⁷ N per metre of length.

nodes.title: Biot-Savart Law & Magnetic Field of Elements
points: Biot-Savart Law gives the magnetic field dB produced by an infinitesimal current element I dl at distance r: dB = (μ₀ / 4π) [I (dl × r̂) / r²] = (μ₀ / 4π) (I dl sinθ / r²).
Constant μ₀ / 4π = 10⁻⁷ T·m/A (or Wb/A·m).
Magnetic field of an infinitely long straight conductor carrying current I at perpendicular distance R: B = μ₀ I / (2πR).
Magnetic field of a semi-infinite straight conductor (at one end): B = μ₀ I / (4πR).
Direction of magnetic field is given by Right-Hand Thumb Rule (thumb points in current direction, curled fingers give direction of B field lines).

nodes.title: Magnetic Field of Circular Coil & Dipole Moment
points: Magnetic field at the CENTRE of a circular coil of N turns and radius R: B_centre = μ₀ N I / (2R).
Magnetic field of an arc of circle subtending angle θ (in radians) at centre: B = (μ₀ I / 4πR) θ.
Magnetic field on the AXIS of a circular coil at distance x from centre: B_axis = (μ₀ N I R²) / [2(R² + x²)³/²].
For points far along axis (x ≫ R): B_axis = μ₀ (N I πR²) / (2π x³) = μ₀ M / (2π x³), where M = NIA is magnetic dipole moment.
Magnetic dipole moment of current loop: M = N I A (SI unit: A·m² or J/T). Vector M points along normal given by right-hand rule.

nodes.title: Ampere's Circuital Law, Solenoid & Toroid
points: Ampere's Circuital Law: Line integral of magnetic induction B around any closed path equals μ₀ times the net enclosed current: ∮ B · dl = μ₀ I_enc.
Long Ideal Solenoid: Magnetic field INSIDE is uniform and parallel to axis: B = μ₀ n I = μ₀ (N/L) I, where n = N/L is turns per unit length.
Magnetic field at the ENDS of a long solenoid: B_end = ½ μ₀ n I = ½ B_inside.
Toroid (endless solenoid bent into a ring of mean radius r): B = μ₀ n I = μ₀ N I / (2πr). Field outside toroid and in central empty space is zero.

formulas.label: Solenoid inside field
formulas.expr: B = μ₀ n I = μ₀ (N/L) I

nodes.title: Torque on Current Loop & Potential Energy
points: Torque on a planar current loop of area A and N turns placed in magnetic field B: τ = M × B ⟹ τ = NIAB sinθ, where θ is angle between M (normal to area) and B.
If α is the angle between plane of the coil and B: τ = NIAB cosα (since θ + α = 90°).
Maximum torque occurs when plane of coil is parallel to B (θ = 90°, α = 0°): τ_max = NIAB.
Potential Energy of magnetic dipole: U = −M · B = −MB cosθ.
Stable equilibrium when θ = 0° (U_min = −MB, τ = 0); Unstable equilibrium when θ = 180° (U_max = +MB, τ = 0).

nodes.title: Moving Coil Galvanometer (MCG) & Radial Field
points: Principle: A current-carrying coil suspended in a magnetic field experiences a deflecting torque.
Deflecting torque: τ_def = NIAB (in radial field, plane of coil is always parallel to B, sinθ = 1).
Restoring torque of phosphor-bronze suspension fibre: τ_rest = c θ, where c is restoring torque per unit twist.
At equilibrium: NIAB = c θ ⟹ I = (c / NAB) θ = K θ (where K is galvanometer constant). Hence I ∝ θ (linear scale).

Role of Radial Magnetic Field: Created using concave cylindrical pole pieces and a soft iron cylinder core. Ensures the deflecting torque is always MAXIMUM (NIAB) and independent of deflection θ, making the scale strictly linear.
Role of Soft Iron Core: Increases magnetic field strength B and makes the magnetic lines strictly radial.

nodes.title: Orbital Magnetic Moment & Bohr Magneton
points: An electron revolving in a circular orbit of radius r with speed v constitutes an electric current: I = e / T = ev / (2πr).
Orbital magnetic dipole moment: M_o = I A = [ev / (2πr)] × πr² = ½ e v r.
In terms of orbital angular momentum L = m_e v r: M_o = [e / (2m_e)] L.
Gyromagnetic Ratio: Ratio of orbital magnetic moment to orbital angular momentum: M_o / L = e / (2m_e) = 8.8 × 10¹⁰ C/kg (constant for all electrons).
Bohr's quantization condition: L = n h / (2π).
Bohr Magneton μ_B: Minimum orbital magnetic moment corresponding to n = 1: μ_B = e h / (4π m_e) = 9.274 × 10⁻²⁴ A·m² (or J/T).

formulas.label: Orbital magnetic moment
formulas.expr: M_o = ½ e v r = [e / (2m_e)] L

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Derivations & Magnetic Formulas
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive expression for magnetic induction at a point on the axis of a circular coil carrying current using Biot-Savart law.
Board Favourite #2: State Ampere's circuital law and use it to derive magnetic field inside a long ideal solenoid: B = μ₀ n I.
Board Favourite #3: Derive expression for the force per unit length between two infinitely long straight parallel conductors: F/L = (μ₀ I₁ I₂)/(2πd).
Board Favourite #4: Explain the construction and working of a Moving Coil Galvanometer and explain the function of the radial magnetic field.
Board Favourite #5: Derive expression for orbital magnetic moment of an electron and obtain the formula for Bohr Magneton.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Traps, Helical Path Shortcuts & Arc Tricks
points: Helical Path of Charged Particle: When v enters B at angle θ (0 < θ < 90°), parallel velocity v_|| = v cosθ causes forward translation; perpendicular velocity v_⊥ = v sinθ causes circular motion.
Radius of helix: r = m v_⊥ / (qB) = m v sinθ / (qB). Pitch of helix: p = v_|| × T = (v cosθ) × [2πm / (qB)].
Magnetic Field Ratio: Ratio of field at centre to field on axis at distance x = R: B_centre / B_axis = [1 + (x/R)²]³/² = [1 + 1]³/² = 2√2 ≈ 2.828.
Biot-Savart Element Trap: Magnetic field along the axis of a current element (θ = 0° or 180°) is strictly ZERO (since sinθ = 0).
Kinetic Energy Trap: In a magnetic field, kinetic energy of a charged particle NEVER changes because F ⊥ v, though momentum vector continuously changes direction.
